title: The shared push-skip action only works on repos whose suite job names match exactly; a repo that adopts it learns the working form where it is written
why: Lane child-ci-q-max measured (coordinator 22:23 and 22:41 CST, relayed; the coordinator calls it checked on real runs): the shared action's suite list is every job key whose job-level `if` is true minus scope, all-jobs-passed, ci-done, push-skip, nightly-skip and the rollup's needs, matched by exact check-run name. On GitHub Actions a matrix job with a constant `name:` keeps its suffix (run 43557726741: `test (1)` to `test (3)`), so it never matches. A `name:` that references `matrix` gets no suffix, and every leg is named exactly the name (run 43557746396, form `name: test${{ matrix.shard == 0 && 'x' || '' }}`). An expression in a step name is evaluated in the jobs API (run 43557764774). The coordinator's earlier premise that a constant name works was wrong.
source: Coordinator 22:23 CST Nov 13 (relayed), lane child-ci-q-max; ruling qmax-skips-push-suite; decision uniform-over-variants.
note: Triage 22:40 CST Nov 13 (rewritten in place): a step, since every repo that adopts the skip hits it. Ask: one ci-hygiene snippet (docs) so repos copy one form, and a line in the push-skip decision, with the measured facts above and q_max and degen's fan-in as worked cases. Optionally a lint that names a suite job whose name carries a matrix suffix or a call prefix. Not started; do after the two child lanes report, so the text carries what they found. No change to the action itself (ruling: a repo changes to fit the tool). Needs a past-ruling and guard-record read before any build.
